message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, or is observed on the nearest weekday when it lands on a weekend, giving you a three‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–3** | New Year’s Day | Jan 1 was a Sunday; the holiday was observed on Monday, Jan 2. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) | Family Day fell on Monday, Feb 20. |
| **Mar 20–22** | Family Day (Ontario) | Family Day fell on Monday, Mar 20. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Good Friday was on Friday, Apr 7. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day fell on Monday, May 22. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day | Canada Day fell on Saturday, Jul 1; it was observed on Monday, Jul 3. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | Labour Day fell on Monday, Sep 4. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving fell on Monday, Oct 9. |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, Nov 11; it was observed on Monday, Nov 13. |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day fell on Monday, Dec 25. |

> **Pro‑Tip:** If you’re building a holiday‑planning app, you might want to flag the *observed* dates (e.g., Canada Day on Jul 3, New Year’s Day on Jan 2) so users see the actual day off.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like province‑specific details or a different format!
